newsitem.title: MEXICO: Serfin exec sees no sale this weekend.
newsitem.headline: Serfin exec sees no sale this weekend.

text.p: The head of Grupo Financiero Serfin, owner of Mexico's third largest bank, said there would be no announcement of a partial sale during the Mexican Bankers Association convention this weekend.

"We are not going to announce anything yet," Adrian Sada, head of Serfin, told reporters late Thursday, countering news reports that a sale with the London-based HSBC Holdings Plc would be announced in this Caribbean resort.
He said talks continued with HSBC, but gave no details. He reaffirmed that only 19.9 percent of Serfin was up for sale.

Sada also said the banking group's 1996 earnings would not show a major loss. "We are not expecting (to report) an important loss," he said, adding there was no attempt to announce results and the Serfin sale at the same time.
Serfin recently received permission from Mexican authorities to report beyond the deadline this week.
Serfin's Director General Adolfo Lagos said it would follow the practice of banking group's Bancomer and Banacci and report part of its earnings under U.S. GAAP accounting standards.
